topic: Phase 4 spike fix #2 — jeep tilt sane
summary: Thomas screenshots showed jeep doing gymnastics — at Turner Valley it was nearly vertical (front-down). Two stacked bugs. (1) Wrong screen-coord conversion: I was using rect.width/vbox.width as x-scale but the SVG uses preserveAspectRatio=xMinYMax slice, which scales uniformly at max(naiveX, naiveY). Replaced naive scale calc with the canonical SVG approach: path.getScreenCTM() + point.matrixTransform(ctm). Handles viewBox + aspect-ratio + parent transforms in one matrix call. (2) No safety cap on displayed angle — chained Bezier S commands produce locally steep tangents that tipped the jeep onto its nose. Capped angle to ±10°. Shipped as commit 0803e3d, theme version 1.0.155.

topic: Phase 4 spike fix #3 — jeep back on screen

Browsers seem to render the path at naive scale when CSS dimensions are explicit. Reverted jeep position calc to use the same naive scale the road visually uses; kept the ±10° angle cap so wild local Bezier tangents (chained S commands) cannot tip the jeep over. topic: Starship belly-flop lander: aero + flaps + layered wind + drifting barge + 38-knob tuning dashboard (UNTESTED)
summary: Second Rockets session; milestone 1 taken from 'a rocket falls' to a Starship belly-flop lander, four commits (ffa9b9b, 3766424, 17cbb5f, 0c482ab), five new files. ENDS UNTESTED -- Thomas ran out of evening before pressing F5, so EVERY line is written and statically checked but NEVER RUN; V0.2.md leads with that. (1) FLIGHT MODEL: thrust with a ramping throttle (binary keys give you nothing to nudge), rotation, finite fuel, camera toggle, flame. (2) THE PHYSICS LESSON when Thomas asked for thrust 'from the rear': applying force at the tail changes NOTHING on its own, because a nozzle pointing down the body axis pushes through the centre of mass and makes no torque -- that's why a real rocket's engine being at the back doesn't tip it over. What matters is GIMBALLING. He chose gimbal + weak RCS. Collider swapped capsule->cylinder: a capsule bottom is a hemisphere so the ship balanced on a point and could never rest upright. (3) THE BIG ONE -- air. Thomas picked the hardest option on all three questions (full belly-flop with working flaps, barge bobbing and drifting on swell, layered gusting wind). Drag split into along-hull and across-hull components dragged separately; across is ~12x along, which makes the flop worth doing, and because the two don't sum to a force pointing straight back along the airflow, TILTING OFF BROADSIDE PRODUCES LIFT -- that glide is the only way to reach a barge not directly below. Weathervane moment (zero nose-first, zero flat, positive between) PLUS an aerodynamic rotational damper, without which the moment is a spring with no dashpot and the ship pendulums forever. Flaps: fore/aft pitches, left/right banks, bite fades as you go vertical exactly where the gimbal takes over -- one key set, two control systems, no mode switch. Mass 5kg->1000kg (with air, 5kg with 4m2 of side profile is a crisp packet). Simulated: terminal 61 m/s belly vs 190+ nose-first, glide ratio peaks ~0.26 at ~25deg off broadside, THE FLIP MUST BE COMMITTED BY ~300m (at 250m it craters), landing costs half the tank. KEY DESIGN FINDING: wind runs everything -- a falling ship moves with the air, so speed x descent time is how far it shoves you (10 m/s over 20s = 200m) against a glide budget of ~120m, so a fixed start point would let the weather decide the run before he touched a key; _place_start() now computes the start from the weather just rolled, cancelling 70% of predicted drift. New atmosphere.gd / world.gd (sea + wave shader + coastline + AnimatableBody3D droneship with sync_to_physics) / rocket_look.gd rewritten as Starship (stainless, weld lines, ogive nose, tiled belly, 4 hinged flaps, 3 Raptors, blue plumes). (4) DASHBOARD: 38 knobs behind Tab; tuning.gd holds values + a SPEC and dashboard.gd builds itself from it, so a new knob is one var + one row. Presets to user://tuning.json. THREE TRAPS AVOIDED: sliders need focus_mode=NONE or they eat WASD and silently break the controls; the pause assist must NOT use get_tree().paused because that stops main.gd processing input and Tab is handled there (freezes the rigid body instead, saving/restoring velocity by hand since freeze discards it); freezing must stay out of _apply_tuning because reset calls it and a frozen body swallows the teleport. Also 'var dashboard: Control' fails at LOAD under static typing -- type such vars as their preloaded script. GOTCHA: git on the Desktop mount leaves undeletable index.lock/HEAD.lock that block the NEXT commit; they can't be rm'd from the sandbox but CAN be renamed (mv index.lock index.lock.stale). NEXT: run it, fix what breaks (suspect the runtime sea shader first), tune by feel via the dashboard, then milestone 2 win/lose -- the data is already tracked, it needs tolerances not new physics.
